title: Biobanking as a Driver of Innovative Molecularly Guided Trials in Rare Cancers
content: Despite the advent of precision oncology, patients with rare tumors continue to be at a therapeutic disadvantage, often referred to as “molecular orphanhood.” The fragmentation of clinical data and the scarcity of high-quality biological samples have historically hindered the translation of genomic advances into clinical practice. In this scenario, dedicated biobanks should no longer be considered simple static repositories of tissue, but rather dynamic drivers of the translational process. This review critically analyzes how the integration of next-generation biobanks is redefining the architecture of molecularly driven clinical trials (basket, umbrella, and adaptive trials). We examine the impact of biobanks in the characterization of complex phenotypes, from central nervous system tumors to ultra-rare sarcomas, highlighting how the availability of annotated samples is an essential prerequisite for the implementation of artificial intelligence algorithms in the discovery of new biomarkers. We also discuss emerging challenges, including harmonizing multi-omics data and integrating liquid biopsy into monitoring protocols. Ultimately, we argue that only a collaborative and centralized biobanking network can transform biological rarity into an opportunity for discovery, bridging the gap between basic research and tailored therapeutic options for patients with rare cancers.
